title: LONGEVITY SURVIVOR — Resolution Gate Data Pack v1.0
frozen_question: Across independent mammalian injury models, is regenerative outcome better separated by the fate, spatial routing and termination of wound-state output than by the lifetime of a single activated-cell marker?
pre_registered_measurement_rules: SCAR_PERSISTENCE_MUST_BE MEASURED IN ECM/ARCHITECTURE AS WELL AS CELLS
original_claim_under_test: REGENERATION = SHORT CONTROLLED WOUND STATE + TIMELY EXIT; SCAR = PERSISTENCE OF THE SAME WOUND STATE

reasons: Adult infarcted heart loses alpha-SMA myofibroblast identity by about day 10-14 while lineage-traced fibroblasts and scar persist in matrifibrocyte-like states.
In full-thickness Acomys skin, dermal alpha-SMA myofibroblasts clear early while a distinct panniculus-associated alpha-SMA scaffold persists for weeks during successful muscle regeneration.
Therefore raw marker half-life does not uniquely classify fibrosis versus regeneration.
topa_result.formula: ENTRY -> WOUND_STATE -> SPATIAL_ROUTING -> HANDOFF_OR_LOCK -> STATE_FATE -> PROFIBROTIC_OUTPUT_TERMINATION -> ARCHITECTURE_OUTCOME

kinetics.observation: lesion gap remains; microglia accumulate/activate
fibronectin-positive bridge present; activated CD68+/SPP1+ microglia occupy lesion; Fn1 repair-state detected
scRNA time-series shows transient repair-state contraction relative to 3 dpi; publication describes Fn1 program as transient
gap refilled; fibronectin signal gone; most microglia regain ramified P2Y12+ homeostatic phenotype
neonatal lesion remains largely scar-free; infiltrating CCR2+ monocyte/macrophage population eliminated

evidence_matrix.adult_control: Adult lesions retain CD68+ P2Y12-negative activated microglia/macrophages through 14 dpi and do not recreate the neonatal scar-free bridge-resolution trajectory.
evidence_matrix.causality: STRONG: microglia depletion impairs bridge formation and axon regrowth; neonatal microglia or peptidase-inhibitor-treated adult microglia improve adult healing.
raw_data_availability: GEO GSE150871: 0/3/5 dpi single-cell RNA-seq; processed and raw files available
Nature source-data spreadsheets supplied with article

kinetics.observation: abundant alpha-SMA+/ScxGFP-negative cells occupy gap; intrinsic Scx-lineage cells proliferate near tendon stubs
scar-associated alpha-SMA/Fb1/Col3a1 transcript program begins transient upregulation
continuous ScxGFP+ neo-tendon present; only limited alpha-SMA staining in neonatal neo-tendon while adult scar remains strongly alpha-SMA/laminin-positive
neonatal scar-associated transcripts return to control levels; intrinsic Scx-lineage cells populate regenerated tendon
neonatal tensile properties restored; collagen remains somewhat developmentally immature but organized

interval_censored_metrics.alpha_SMA_helper_decline: abundant at 3 dpi, strongly reduced by 14 dpi
interval_censored_metrics.scar_transcript_output_exit: begins around 7 dpi and returns to control by 28 dpi

evidence_matrix.adult_control: Adult intrinsic tenocytes do not enter the defect; extrinsic alpha-SMA cells dominate scar tissue and adult function remains impaired.
evidence_matrix.causality: MODERATE_TO_STRONG: lineage tracing establishes handoff to intrinsic tenocytes; macrophage depletion impairs neonatal regeneration; TGF-beta signaling is required for neonatal tenocyte recruitment. Direct selective manipulation of alpha-SMA-helper EXIT is still missing.

evidence_matrix.species_model: adult Acomys cahirinus 2-mm ear punch versus scar-forming Mus

kinetics.observation: myofibroblasts appear in both Acomys and Mus
Acomys wound closes and regenerative blastema differentiates; EDA-fibronectin/myofibroblast program remains transient
Acomys myofibroblasts resolve while Mus myofibroblasts persist
Acomys restores pigmentation and complex tissue without scar

evidence_matrix.causal_perturbation: Chronic verteporfin inhibition of nuclear YAP-TEAD prolongs Acomys myofibroblast persistence, alters cell fate/patterning and converts regenerative healing toward fibrosis.

interval_censored_metrics.regenerative_MF_window: approximately weeks 1-2 with resolution over weeks 3-4

evidence_matrix.raw_data_availability: Article/supplemental information available; authors state additional supporting data available on reasonable request.

evidence_matrix.species_model: adult Acomys cahirinus versus CD-1 Mus, 1-cm full-thickness dorsal skin wounds
evidence_matrix.outcome: Acomys regenerates skin appendages and panniculus; Mus forms stable collagenous scar

kinetics.observation: approximately 75% of upper wound-zone cells are alpha-SMA-positive in both Mus and Acomys; initial induction is therefore not regeneration-specific
Mus retains intense alpha-SMA throughout wound bed; Acomys upper dermal alpha-SMA effectively disappears while a strong lower alpha-SMA bridge emerges between cut panniculus ends
Mus dermal myofibroblasts have virtually disappeared but uniform collagenous scar persists; Acomys upper dermal myofibroblasts are cleared while panniculus alpha-SMA bridge remains intense
Mus remains collagenous despite low alpha-SMA; Acomys panniculus-associated alpha-SMA bridge remains high
Acomys panniculus muscle architecture regenerates

killer_observations: Mus proves scar persistence can outlive dermal alpha-SMA myofibroblast persistence.
Acomys proves long-lived alpha-SMA occupancy can coexist with regeneration when spatially routed to a muscle-regenerative scaffold.
kinetics.quantitative_anchor: At day 7, authors estimate approximately 75% alpha-SMA-positive cells in the upper wound zone in both Mus and Acomys; ImageJ intensity measurements are reported across weeks 1-5.

kinetics.species_model: adult mouse myocardial infarction with Tcf21/Postn/Acta2 lineage tracing
kinetics.state: resident cardiac fibroblast -> activated fibroblast -> alpha-SMA myofibroblast -> matrifibrocyte

kinetics.observation: resident fibroblast proliferation peaks; population expands approximately 3.5-fold
alpha-SMA myofibroblast state first observed
myofibroblast state maximal; abundant ECM production
proliferation stops and alpha-SMA declines
lineage-traced cells transition toward stable matrifibrocyte state
alpha-SMA absent from lineage-traced fibroblasts while mature scar persists

kinetics.killer_observation: Marker-state EXIT does not equal fibrosis EXIT; the same lineage remains in scar in a different stable state and ECM remains mature.
kinetics.mechanical_feedback: Blocking collagen maturation with beta-aminopropionitrile/LOX inhibition prolongs alpha-SMA expression to day 14, supporting coupling between ECM maturation and fibroblast state transitions.

kinetics.species_model: P1 mouse LAD ligation; WT versus fibroblast-specific or myeloid-specific Erbb4 knockout

kinetics.observation: baseline infarct scar quantified; fibroblast-Erbb4 KO comparable to WT, myeloid-Erbb4 KO approximately 2-fold larger than WT
scar size decreases approximately 6-fold from day 4 in both WT and fibroblast-KO, but fibroblast-KO retains significantly larger scar
fibroblast-KO retains larger scar, lower capillary density and higher Col1a1; myeloid-KO also remains larger with altered Mmp2/Mmp9
regeneration nearly complete; fibroblast-KO retains a small but significantly larger residual scar; myeloid-KO converges toward WT residual scar

kinetics.killer_observation: Scar-resolution kinetics can be altered by fibroblast/myeloid ERBB4 perturbation without a matching change in cardiomyocyte cell-cycle activity, experimentally separating RESOLUTION from PROLIFERATION.
kinetics.status_note: PREPRINT; not yet peer-reviewed. Do not promote to settled mechanism.

supported: Regenerative programs frequently include a transient wound-response state rather than avoiding wound/fibrotic programs entirely.
Successful regeneration repeatedly requires handoff from initial stabilization to tissue-specific rebuilding.
Cell-state duration contains information but is not sufficient without state identity, compartment, lineage fate and ECM-output persistence.
Fibrotic memory can persist in ECM and in post-myofibroblast cell states after canonical alpha-SMA marker loss.
The same canonical wound marker can represent distinct functions depending on spatial routing and downstream fate.
refuted: A universal numerical alpha-SMA half-life threshold separates regeneration from scar.
Persistent scar requires indefinite persistence of alpha-SMA-positive myofibroblasts.
Long-lived alpha-SMA-positive cells are necessarily fibrotic.
Regenerative tissues simply fail to activate fibrotic/wound-response machinery.
cross_system_results.highest_value_next_variable: PROFIBROTIC_OUTPUT_OCCUPANCY(t): collagen deposition/crosslinking, periostin, matrix alignment/stiffness and MMP:TIMP balance, tracked alongside lineage-resolved cell-state occupancy and final architecture.

already_known_in_field: Fibrosis resolution literature already recognizes myofibroblast apoptosis/dedifferentiation/reprogramming plus ECM degradation as separable processes.
Acomys literature already emphasizes transient activation of fibrotic pathways during regeneration.
Therefore JANUS must not claim discovery of the general concept of fibrosis resolution or transient myofibroblasts.
novelty_check.potentially_useful_contribution: A falsification-first cross-tissue kinetic alignment that explicitly separates marker lifetime, lineage fate, spatial compartment and ECM-output lifetime, and uses counterexamples to reject half-life-only models.

minimum_data_needed_for_next_step: Acomys ear: numeric Acta2+/Myh11- volume values by week and verteporfin condition.
Acomys full-thickness skin: ImageJ alpha-SMA intensity values by spatial compartment and time point, ideally raw per-animal values.
Neonatal tendon: alpha-SMA cell abundance at intermediate times between d3 and d14 and lineage fate after marker loss.
Neonatal spinal cord: lesion-level Fn1/fibronectin and P2Y12/SPP1/CD68 quantitative values across 3/5/7 dpi, linked to GSE150871 cell-state proportions.
Adult heart: quantitative transition probabilities/occupancy from activated fibroblast to myofibroblast to matrifibrocyte plus collagen/crosslinking metrics.
2026 neonatal heart preprint: raw scar-area values at 4/7/10/21 dpi by genotype and matching Col1a1/MMP/capillary metrics.

communication_boundary.safe_statement: Across several mammalian injury models, existing data suggest that regenerative versus fibrotic outcome is not classified by the lifetime of a single activated-cell marker. A more testable cross-tissue model tracks state fate, spatial routing, handoff to resident rebuilding, and persistence of profibrotic ECM output.
